title: Farm-scale anaerobic storage and aerobic feed-out reference outcomes for switchgrass and reed canarygrass
citation: Williams, S. D., & Shinners, K. J. (2014). Farm-scale anaerobic storage and aerobic stability of high dry matter perennial grasses as biomass feedstocks. Biomass and Bioenergy, 64, 91–98. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.biombioe.2014.03.037
source_locations: Table 1, article p. 3: dry matter concentrations and anaerobic/aerobic dry-matter losses
Table 3, article p. 5: cellulose and hemicellulose entering storage and constituent recovery
Table 5, article p. 6: aerobic-exposure heating degree days
Methods §§2.1–2.3, article pp. 2–4: harvest, storage, replication and aerobic exposure
geography: Wisconsin, USA. The authors acknowledge staff of the University of Wisconsin Arlington Agricultural Research Station; exact plot location is not explicitly stated in the methods.
license: The article states © 2014 Elsevier Ltd. All rights reserved; no open reuse license was identified. This repository contains attributed factual values only, not source text or figures. External redistribution rights are not asserted.
material_scope: Mature, seed-ripening switchgrass (Panicum virgatum cv. Shawnee) and reed canarygrass (Phalaris arundinacea cv. Palaton), harvested in 2010 after one day of field wilting and chopped to a theoretical 12 mm cut. Switchgrass had low- and high-DM treatments; only low-DM reed canarygrass was harvested because rain prevented the high-DM treatment.
experimental_conditions: Farm-scale anaerobic silo bags: one bag per crop, opened after 222 d for switchgrass and 230 d for reed canarygrass. Six replicate mesh-bag subsample parcels were used per storage treatment. The aerobic stability test placed material in loosely filled, uncovered 200-L barrels indoors in a ventilated shed for 2 or 7 d, at final DM density 80–90 kg/m3. Four barrels were filled per treatment; Table 5 does not state the replicate count for its reported heating-degree-day means. Inoculated material received approximately 400000 cfu/g Lactobacillus buchneri and 100000 cfu/g Pediococcus pentosaceus.
data_scope: Six individual crop × treatment × DM-class rows, excluding the article's pooled treatment and pooled DM summaries. Table 1 values: stored/removed DM concentration, anaerobic storage DM loss, and additional DM loss after 2 and 7 d aerobic exposure; reported significance letters retained for applicable cells. Table 3 values: cellulose and hemicellulose concentrations entering storage on a DM basis and source-defined constituent recovery fractions. Table 5 values: dry matter at start of aerobic exposure and heating degree days at shallow/deep positions after 2/7 d.
limitations: Reference-only; not Dutch roadside grass, not a GreenHub runtime input/default, and not a storage calibration. Crop species, maturity, harvest, chopping, storage structure and high-DM cellulosic-feedstock purpose differ from the project's wet roadside grass.
The trial used one farm-scale silo bag per species and one harvest year; six mesh-bag subsamples per treatment do not constitute independent silo replicates.
The aerobic exposure test is sequential after anaerobic storage. It is not a separate aerobic-storage scenario and its 2/7-day endpoints must not be interpreted as a standalone aerobic storage curve.
Loss data are endpoint treatment means. No kinetic function, interpolation, annualization, GreenHub transfer coefficient, or emissions inventory is inferred.
The Table 5 dry-matter concentrations differ slightly from Table 1 removal values; both source-table values are preserved separately rather than reconciled.
Table 3 recovery fractions can exceed one for hemicellulose; these are source-reported analytical recovery ratios, not mass-balance closure guarantees.
Table 5 heating degree days are reported by the source in °C; the CSV labels the accumulated quantity as °C·day. Table 5 replicate count is not specified.

The source reports additional LSD statistics and pooled treatment/DM summaries that are not transcribed. Only the six individual treatment rows and source significance-group letters shown alongside those rows are included.
conversion_or_processing: Direct transcription of six unpooled treatment rows from Tables 1, 3 and 5. DM concentration is preserved as g/kg material as reported; losses are preserved as g/kg DM; recovery values are dimensionless fractions. Heating-degree-day values are carried over numerically and labeled as accumulated °C·day. No conversion, interpolation, fitting, imputation, averaging, or activation was performed.
uncertainty: The article reports six replicate mesh-bag subsample parcels per storage treatment and significance groups/LSD statistics for Tables 1 and 3; cell-level SD/SE is not reported in these tables. Table 5 replicate count and uncertainty are not stated. Empty significance-group fields mean no group letter is shown for that source-table cell, not zero or not measured.
